data.content_ref: inline:exp-hist:{"target": "17abc40d78973c8702f6ebf724a089d996f442d21e098baf7092be922226080c", "seq": 1, "objection": "The target's defense collapses because it relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) to justify preference without induction, yet the Tichý/Miller proof (which the target acknowledges as a countercondition) demonstrates that verisimilitude cannot be formally defined or compared in rich languages. If the metric for 'better-corroborated' is logically incoherent or undefinable, then the claim that preferring such theories is a 'rational guess' based on 'logical content' becomes empty; one cannot rationally prefer X over Y based on a property P if P cannot be determined to hold for X more than Y. Thus, the target fails to show the preference is defensible on Popper's own terms, as those terms require logical rigor which the verisimilitude solution lacks.", "outcome": "raised and not answered; the target's status did not move"}
